facts: arXiv cs.SE listing for 2026-08 was scanned via listing page skip=300&show=250; the skip=150 chunk returned HTTP 400 and could not be retrieved, so mid-window (Aug 10-19) coverage relies on keyword search rather than exhaustive listing enumeration.

arXiv:2608.23628 (Aug 23, 2026) introduces AFT-Bench, a controlled interface-intervention framework holding task, backend, initial state, injected failure, agent and model fixed while varying only the tool interface exposed to the agent.

arXiv:2608.21208 (Aug 21, 2026) tested specification-driven Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration across five agents (Amazon Kiro, Google Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor); stage 1 covered 1,006 PL/SQL files (623 regenerated, 380 executed), stage 2 covered 1,802 Oracle scripts.

arXiv:2608.21298 (Aug 21, 2026) is a controlled crossover experiment with 34 participants inspecting textual requirements with and without LLM support; LLM support significantly reduced smell-detection accuracy with no significant effect on classification or task duration.

arXiv:2608.23651 (Aug 24, 2026) reports greedy decoding reproduced a failed tool call token-for-token on 19% of items after failure versus 0% before, and attributes 83% of the effect to the failed call's surface form rather than to semantic failure marking.

arXiv:2608.25241 (Aug 26, 2026) analyzed 441 repositories with a four-level maturity model (RAMP) validated at 97% accuracy against human annotation; agent adoption raised commit volume 28-38% at all levels, but cognitive complexity rose ~53% (static-analysis warnings 1.7x) without committed AI configuration versus ~27% with it.
Several strong 2026 failure-mode papers surfaced but fall outside the 21-day window (2608.04278 Aug 4, 2608.06503 Aug 6) and were excluded from candidate records.
inferences: The catalog's K14 (external side effects not undone by code rollback) and I04 (destructive commands from bad inference) both presume the agent knows an effect occurred; arXiv:2608.23628 characterizes the prior condition where the agent cannot determine whether the effect committed at all, which implies a different practical response (interface-level postcondition/idempotency affordances rather than permission gating).

arXiv:2608.21298 inverts the direction of catalog J05: J05 covers humans over-trusting AI *output*, whereas here humans miss defects in their own artifact because the LLM did not flag them, i.e. AI silence read as clearance. The affected artifact is the requirements document, placing it near category A/J rather than code review.

arXiv:2608.21208's degradation is confounded with a narrow domain (SQL dialect migration) and with agent-specific spec formats; the portability finding is likely real but the effect sizes should not be generalized to natural-language design specs without further evidence.

arXiv:2608.23651 materially changes the recommended response to catalog G06: if the failed call's verbatim surface form in the transcript is itself the driver, then 'instruct the agent to root-cause before retrying' is weaker than transcript hygiene (replacing verbatim failed calls with runtime-generated descriptions, or decoder-level suppression of previously-failed strings).

arXiv:2608.25241 supplies the first repository-scale conditional evidence for catalog E10: debt acceleration after agent adoption is not unconditional but roughly halves when AI configuration is version-controlled, which upgrades committed AI config from hygiene to a measured mitigation.

records.title: ツール応答の消失により、外部副作用が確定したか未確定かをAgentが判別できない
records.summary: Agentがツールを呼び出し、外部システム側の副作用は確定したのに応答だけが失われた場合、確定状態と未確定状態がAgentから見て区別できなくなる。両者は本来まったく異なる継続動作(再試行 vs 前進)を要求するため、Agentは重複実行か停止のどちらかに倒れる。呼び出しがスキーマ的に妥当(callable)であることと、結果状態を判定して安全に継続できること(operable)は別物であり、失敗はモデル能力ではなくツールInterface設計に起因する。AFT-Benchはタスク・Backend・初期状態・注入する障害・Agent・Modelを固定しInterfaceのみを変える統制実験でこれを分離した。

evidence.title: Callability Is Not Operability: Controlled Interface Interventions for LLM Agents
evidence.summary: Introduces AFT-Bench, a controlled interface-intervention framework, and shows a tool call can be perfectly valid yet leave the agent unable to determine what to do next; committed and uncommitted states become indistinguishable when external effects commit but responses are lost. Proposes Agent-First Tooling: selective capability discovery, execution lifecycle and recovery, explicit external-effect semantics, machine-readable results, postcondition verification.

records.notes: Checked against K14 (external side effects not reversible by code rollback), I04 (destructive command from bad inference), C08 (env/flag/runtime differences overlooked), G06 (blind command retry). All four presume the agent knows what happened; this is the prior epistemic failure where commit status itself is unobservable. Practical response also differs: interface-level postcondition verification and explicit effect semantics rather than permission gating or rollback planning.

records.title: ある製品向けに書かれた仕様がAgent製品を跨ぐと成立せず、実装品質が製品依存で崩壊する
records.summary: Spec-driven開発で作成した仕様Artifactは、作成元のAgent製品に暗黙適合しており、別製品のAgentへ持ち込むと大幅な品質劣化を起こす。5製品(Kiro/Gemini/Copilot/Claude Code/Cursor)を跨いだ実測で、Kiro由来仕様をGeminiに投入した最悪ケースはToken F1 0.035、SQL構文妥当性2.33%まで落ちた。仕様のサイズ自体は実装品質を予測せず、仕様の書き直しは改善する一方、圧縮の効果は製品間で一貫しない。「仕様はVendor中立な資産」という前提が成り立たないことを示す。

evidence.title: Specification Portability Across LLM Development Agents: Cross-Agent Compatibility in Specification-Driven Software Migration
evidence.summary: Two-stage study: 1,006 PL/SQL files (623 regenerated, 380 executed in PostgreSQL 16), then 1,802 Oracle scripts across five agents. Cross-agent transfer produces substantial agent-dependent degradation; specification size alone does not predict implementation quality; rewriting substantially improves performance while compression gives inconsistent benefits.

records.notes: Checked against H04 (agents interpret the same spec/interface differently) and K08 (session/skill formats fragmented per provider), D15 (skill owner/model/runtime unknown). H04 concerns concurrent divergent interpretation inside one project; K08 concerns session and skill format fragmentation, not spec-artifact fidelity. This is spec-artifact non-portability at handoff/migration time with a distinct response (renormalize or rewrite specs when switching agent products, and measure rather than assume transfer). Confidence held at medium because the study domain is narrow (Oracle-to-PostgreSQL SQL migration).

records.title: LLMを検査支援に使うと、要求文書のSmell検出精度がかえって下がる
records.summary: 人間が書いた要求仕様のInspectionでLLM支援を併用すると、欠陥(Requirements smell)の検出精度が有意に低下する。分類精度と作業時間には有意差がないため、時間短縮と引き換えでもない純粋な検出漏れである。LLMが指摘しなかった箇所を「問題なし」と読む false assurance が働き、検査者の探索が早期に打ち切られる。さらに最初からLLM支援ありで学習した被験者は学習効果自体が減衰しており、初学者の検査技能獲得を遅らせる。

evidence.title: Human-AI Collaboration in Requirements Engineering: Evidence of the Negative Effect of LLMs on Requirements Inspection
evidence.summary: Controlled crossover experiment with 34 participants inspecting textual specifications with and without LLM assistance. LLM support significantly reduced smell-detection accuracy with no significant effect on classification or task duration; learning effects were present across periods but reduced when LLM support was used from the beginning.

records.notes: Checked against J05 (over-trusting AI and missing plausible errors), J04 (review degenerating into formal approval), J08 (skill atrophy), J09 (juniors losing learning opportunities). J04/J05 concern humans reviewing AI-produced output; here the artifact under inspection is human-authored and the AI is the review aid, so the failure is AI silence read as clearance - the opposite direction, with a different response (keep an unaided inspection pass, and do not introduce LLM aids to novices before baseline skill is established). Overlaps J08/J09 on the learning-effect finding; controller may prefer to split that half into an update on J09.

records.title: 失敗したCommandをTranscriptに残すこと自体が、同一失敗の再実行を誘発する
records.summary: 失敗したツール呼び出しとError messageを文脈に残す標準的なやり方が、同じ呼び出しの再生成確率を押し上げる。原因はError messageの意味理解の失敗ではなく、失敗した呼び出しの表層形が文脈内で顕著になり再生成されやすくなることにある。損害の83%は表層形に帰属し、失敗という意味付けの寄与は一貫しない。対策も「原因分析してから再試行せよ」という指示ではなく、逐語のCommandをRuntime生成の説明文へ置換する(損害の76%除去)、あるいはDecoder側で既失敗文字列を禁止する、というTranscript衛生の側に移る。

evidence.title: Feedback That Backfires: Why Small Language Model Agents Repeat the Call They Just Watched Fail
evidence.summary: Six model checkpoints (135M-1.7B) across four families, in simulated tool calling and MBPP program repair. Corrective gain was negative across all models (about -1.03 nats/token), yet repetition probability rose from 0.06 to 0.54 under greedy decoding on fixed candidate sets; greedy decoding reproduced failed calls token-for-token on 19% of items post-failure vs 0% before. Failed-call surface form accounts for 83% of the effect; replacing verbatim calls with runtime-generated descriptions removes 76%.

records.notes: Symptom is exactly catalog G06 (re-running the same failed command without root-cause analysis), so this is not a new problem. It is an update because the mechanism is relocated from 'agent skipped analysis' to 'verbatim failed call in context is mechanically more likely to be regenerated', which changes the recommended response from instruction-level (analyze before retry) to harness-level transcript hygiene and decoder-level suppression. Confidence low because the evidence covers only 135M-1.7B parameter models; frontier coding-agent generalization is untested and should be stated as a limitation in any catalog text.

records.title: Agent導入後の負債蓄積速度は、AI設定をRepositoryにCommitしているかで約2倍変わる
records.summary: Coding agent導入によるCommit量増加(28-38%)は設定の有無に関わらず得られる一方、品質コストは分岐する。AI設定をVersion管理していないRepositoryではCognitive complexityが約53%増、静的解析警告が1.7倍に増えたのに対し、Commit済み設定があるRepositoryでは複雑度増加が約27%に留まった。つまりE10の「生成量に比例した負債蓄積」は無条件ではなく、AI設定のVersion管理という具体的な調整変数を持つ。441 Repositoryの観察研究であり因果ではない点に注意が必要。

evidence.title: A Few Pages of Markdown: Committed AI Configuration and Lower Quality Cost after Coding-Agent Adoption
evidence.summary: Introduces RAMP (Repository AI Maturity Profile), a four-level cumulative maturity model over version-controlled artifacts, across 441 repositories, validated against independent human annotation at 97% accuracy on held-out samples. Velocity rose 28-38% in commits at all maturity levels; cognitive complexity rose ~53% with static-analysis warnings 1.7x without committed AI configuration, versus ~27% with it.

records.notes: Not a new problem: E10 already states that technical debt accumulates faster in proportion to AI generation volume. Material change is the quantified moderator - committed AI configuration roughly halves the complexity increase at equal velocity gain - which promotes 'commit your AI configuration' from D-category hygiene to a measured E10 mitigation and gives the catalog a concrete metric pair (cognitive complexity, static-analysis warning rate) for monitoring. Also relevant to D04/D12 as counter-evidence that configuration files are not merely instruction debt. Observational design, so association not causation.
